Root question: generative pipeline for discovery of single phase immersion coolants
Option record: {\"id\":\"immersion-coolants\",\"title\":\"Generative search for single-phase immersion coolants\",\"summary\":\"Data-centre immersion cooling needs dielectric liquids with low viscosity, high thermal conductivity and heat capacity, a low dielectric constant and a high flash point. PFAS rules and the end of Novec production are pushing the field towards PFAS-free hydrocarbons and esters. Study whether a generative search over molecules and mixtures finds candidates that beat known commercial single-phase fluids on a cooling figure of merit. More compute buys more candidates checked by GPU molecular dynamics after predictor filtering, and longer simulations per candidate. Score against measured viscosity, thermal conductivity and dielectric data for known fluids held out of training, never against the predictors themselves.\",\"root_link\":\"SAME: a concrete version of the asker's line, kept on discovery and on transport properties (viscosity, thermal conductivity).\",\"compute_open\":\"Candidates checked by GPU molecular dynamics (about 10^2 to 10^4) and simulation length per candidate. Unknown: whether the hit rate against known commercial fluids keeps rising with more candidates, or whether predictor and force-field error caps it.\",\"sequential\":\"not given\",\"source_urls\":[\"https://espace2.etsmtl.ca/id/eprint/31955/\",\"https://blog.se.com/datacenter/2026/05/22/pfas-phase-out-liquid-cooling-us-data-center-operators-must-do/\",\"https://opencompute.org/documents/ocp-acs-immersion-requirements-rev-2-v1-00-pdf\"]}
Card:
card:question: Does verifying more candidate coolants with GPU molecular dynamics keep raising the best figure of merit above known commercial single-phase fluids, or does it plateau?
card:hypothesis: Predictor-filtered molecular dynamics finds PFAS-free esters or hydrocarbons that beat commercial coolants [orgmol], and more candidates keep improving the best one.
card:sequential_part: One trajectory runs timestep by timestep; verifying a thousand candidates serially chains that work a thousand times.
card:method: none
card:if_lever: Best cooling figure of merit keeps climbing with candidates verified, so more compute keeps finding fluids that beat commercial ones.
card:if_not: Best figure of merit plateaus by a few hundred candidates, because predictor filtering and ~10% force-field error cap how high MD-ranked fluids score.
card:test_summary: Generate a million PFAS-free esters and hydrocarbons, ML-filter to a ranked shortlist, MD-verify the top 100, 300, then 1000 candidates' viscosity and thermal conductivity, and compare their cooling figure of merit to commercial fluids.
card:closest_prior: Org-Mol ML-screened six million esters and experimentally validated two; it never MD-verified hundreds-to-thousands of candidates at once.
card:left_open: No study measures whether the best MD-ranked coolant keeps improving as the number of MD-verified candidates grows from 100 to 10,000.
card:anchor: MD pipeline reproduces n-hexadecane thermal conductivity 0.1444 W/m/K and viscosity 2.95 mPa/s near 300 K before scoring candidates.
card:limits: Result is a ranking and hit rate, not absolute fluid accuracy; one fluid class, no mixtures, no synthesis or lifetime testing.

Criteria:
stakes: Take the two outcomes this test predicts, as measured here and within the limits in scope_gap. 5 = whichever occurs, a choice someone faces (what to buy, build, collect or scale next) changes, and the test measures the quantity that choice depends on; 3 = the outcomes bear on that choice only through a step this test does not check (a stand-in system, simulation to reality, a single model), or one outcome is already much more likely than the other; 1 = neither outcome would change anything. Do not score how famous the field is or how close it is to the root question.
lever: Could the result tell if_lever from if_not, with compute the only thing that changed? Check four conditions: (a) the predicted difference between if_lever and if_not is larger than what noise_rule says run-to-run noise can produce; (b) compute_axis spans at least 10×; (c) the varied quantity is bought with compute, not with more data, labels or people (when restructuring.method is not none: the arms run on the same hardware and differ only in method); (d) inputs that could also explain the difference are in held_fixed. 5 = all four hold; 3 = one fails or cannot be told from the plan; 1 = two or more fail, or the measured quantity is not the one the question asks about.
verifiable: What is the measured outcome scored against? 5 = an exact or planted truth that does not come from the method under test (a simulation's hidden true run, an exact success flag, a formal checker, planted items), and the setup first reproduces a published number within a stated tolerance; 3 = labels from a model or human rater with an agreement check, or exact truth with no reproduction step; 1 = nothing independent of the method's own output.
open: Does the closest published result already answer this question over this range? 5 = the quoted prior stops short of this range or asks a different question, and the plan states the gap; 3 = the prior answers part of it (a narrower range, a related system), or no prior is named; 1 = the quoted prior already answers it. Reusing published tools, models or benchmarks does not lower this score.
reshape: Does the plan remove a step-after-step dependency that one answer waits on, rather than run independent work side by side? 5 = restructuring names the dependency, why it need not run in order and how the plan computes it at the same time; condition says what must hold for that to pay off; condition_phase measures it before the main spend; and the closest prior does not already do this for this system; 3 = it removes a dependency, but condition is missing or is not measured before the main spend; 2 = it parallelises only within each step (splitting a large state across GPUs) or regroups and rebalances independent work (batching unfinished runs, load balancing, lower precision), leaving the chain in order; 1 = independent copies side by side, or one job per GPU, is the only parallelism, or the plan rebuilds a parallel version the closest prior already reports for this system. Reusing a method published for a different system does not lower this score.
baseline: Is the gain timed against the strongest ways to get the same answer without the plan's method? Check four conditions: (a) baseline_sequential is tuned (compiled, vectorised or multithreaded code, or a published optimised code), not a plain interpreted loop; (b) baseline_copies is timed on the same GPUs; (c) anchor checks the parallel result against the sequential one within a stated tolerance; (d) a named phase times every arm as time or dollars to one answer, so the gain is measured, not only modelled. 5 = all four hold; 3 = one fails or cannot be told from the plan; 1 = two or more fail. NA when restructuring.method is none.

Return only one JSON value, with no other text, that matches this JSON Schema:
{\"type\":\"object\",\"properties\":{\"scores\":{\"type\":\"array\",\"items\":{\"type\":\"object\",\"properties\":{\"criterion\":{\"type\":\"string\"},\"value\":{\"anyOf\":[{\"type\":\"integer\",\"minimum\":1,\"maximum\":5},{\"type\":\"string\",\"enum\":[\"NA\"]}]},\"ref\":{\"type\":\"string\",\"description\":\"\\"card:<field>\\" for the card field that decides the score, or \\"plan:<field path>\\" when no card field carries it.\"},\"reason\":{\"type\":\"string\"}},\"required\":[\"criterion\",\"value\",\"ref\",\"reason\"]}},\"decides_by\":{\"type\":\"string\",\"description\":\"A phase id, or \\"none\\".\"},\"decides_by_reason\":{\"type\":\"string\"}},\"required\":[\"scores\",\"decides_by\",\"decides_by_reason\"]}"

A phase only reproduces published number, or measures throughput question does not ask about, does not count. Need decide from text.

Let's parse card/plan. Need criteria.
